hint.emptyAssemblyBody: Its plates apply to other variants of the model, which is normal: for this vehicle {{available}} of {{total}} assemblies have parts. Pick another, or untick hide to see the empty ones.

language.note: The language of the application's own text. The catalogue's own words — criterion names, assembly names, part descriptions — come from the tree and are chosen below.
language.catalogueNote: Criterion names, assembly names and the menu come from langue/<code>/. Changing this reopens the tree, which takes a moment — the vocabulary and the menu are read again.

settings.title: Settings
settings.lede: dialogysx ships no vehicle data. Point it at a tree built with dialogysx import — served over HTTP with Range support, or a folder on this machine.
settings.httpHint: Any host that honours Range: a static server, or an S3 bucket with public read and CORS. The catalogue is sampled by byte range, so the multi-gigabyte files are never downloaded.
settings.noFsaHint: This browser has no File System Access API — it is Chromium-only today. Use an HTTP tree instead.
settings.folderHint: An imported tree, or a mounted disc's dialogys/data directory. Nothing is uploaded; files are read straight off disk.
settings.needsPermission: — needs permission again after a reload
settings.noTreeHint: Build one from mounted Dialogys discs, here in the browser — no command line. You will be asked for a target folder and then for each disc in turn.
settings.reopenNote: A URL is reopened automatically next time. A folder is remembered too, but browsers drop its permission on reload, so it needs one click to grant access again.
settings.partNamesResolved: Resolved from {{country}}. Part descriptions ship per country rather than per language — several countries share one language, and each tariff names only what is sold there, so coverage is partial by design.
settings.partNamesMissing: None in this tree. Import the part-names component to get them; without it parts show a reference and no description.

about.what: A parts catalogue and repair-documentation browser for Renault and Dacia vehicles: pick a model and a vehicle, and it shows the exploded drawings with the part numbers that fit, plus the workshop manuals and technical notes that apply.
about.howItRuns: It runs entirely in the browser. Nothing is uploaded and there is no server component — the catalogue's own (position, length) addressing is read with HTTP Range requests, or straight off a folder on this machine, so the multi-gigabyte data files are sampled rather than downloaded.
about.cleanRoom: A clean-room reimplementation of Renault's Dialogys 7.5.6, written from its data formats. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Renault.
about.dataTitle: The data is not included, and not redistributable
about.dataBody: The catalogue, the drawings and the repair documents are Renault/Dacia's. This program reads a tree you build yourself from discs you have; it ships no vehicle data and gives you no right to pass any on.
about.verifyBody: The applicability rules were recovered by reading the original program, and they hold across all 41,758 plates in the catalogue. That is not the same as a verified parts list: no result here has yet been checked against an independently known answer. Confirm a part number before you buy or fit it.
about.licenceSuffix: . Provided as is, without warranty of any kind.

import.title: Import from discs
import.noFsa: This browser has no File System Access API. Use the CLI importer instead.
import.targetLead: Choose an empty folder to build the tree in. It needs write access — a different prompt from the read-only one the catalogue uses.
import.targetHint: Mount your ISOs first (double-click each one). You will be asked for them one at a time, and can stop whenever you like.
import.writing: Writing {{kind}} — do not close this tab.
import.betweenHint: Mount the next ISO now if you have one. Nothing is lost by stopping: the tree is usable for whatever has been imported, and you can come back to it later.
import.finishedHint: The manifest is written, so the app can read this tree. Run dialogysx verify -d <folder> if you want the indexes checked — the browser importer does not count keys.
